assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm heterogeneity and selection into exporting changed how trade economists think about gains from trade, reallocation and productivity. It reshaped both theory and empirical work, and it links to micro data on firms. The impact is broad and durable.
assessment.attribution: Melitz (2003) is the central contribution. Helpman's work with Melitz and Yeaple on exporting versus FDI, and his broader heterogeneous-firm research, supports a second laureate. Redding is important for quantitative extensions, but his role is more derivative of the original framework, so he is not proposed.
assessment.maturity: More than twenty years of confirmation: the framework is standard in textbooks, empirical trade and policy analysis. Krugman's 2008 prize covered new trade theory and geography, but this is a distinct, later advance.
uncertainties: Committee view on overlap with the 2008 trade prize.
Whether Helpman or Redding is the better co-laureate.
Helpman also appears in B013, and any overlapping credit would need sorting out.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This work formalised how constitutions, electoral rules and state capacity shape fiscal policy and economic outcomes. It created a coherent empirical and theoretical research program in political economics, with large influence on development and public economics.
assessment.attribution: Persson and Tabellini are the joint originators of the constitutional and electoral-rules program. Besley and Persson drove the state-capacity and fiscal-capacity strand. Both strands are close and credit is fairly clear, though they are not identical lines of work.
assessment.maturity: Decades of work, with core papers and books from the 1990s and 2000s that have been replicated and extended. The 2024 prize on institutions and prosperity partly covers neighbouring themes.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2024 institutions prize.
Whether to include Besley or limit the prize to Persson and Tabellini.
The degree of causal identification in cross-country constitutional work.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The legal-origins and investor-protection research established a large empirical agenda linking law, finance and development. It drew on newly assembled cross-country data. It is among the most cited bodies of work in economics and shaped policy and scholarship.
assessment.attribution: The core papers are by La Porta, Lopez-de-Silanes, Shleifer and Vishny. A three-person limit forces the omission of Vishny, who is credited with the 1990s core papers, which is a real attribution cost.
assessment.maturity: The work dates from the late 1990s and has had ample time to be tested. Later research has challenged the legal-origins causal interpretation and the doing-business variants.
uncertainties: The causal interpretation of legal origins is disputed.
Omission of Vishny under the three-name cap.
Shleifer's other work and controversies, which are not merit evidence but may affect committee dynamics.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nominal rigidities, Calvo pricing and the New Keynesian framework underpin modern monetary policy analysis and central bank practice. The intellectual and practical impact is very large.
assessment.attribution: Credit is spread over eight names across several strands: Calvo pricing, the Taylor rule, the Woodford synthesis, Galí's empirical and theoretical work, and the Christiano-Eichenbaum-Evans medium-scale models with Smets. The three-name cap makes it hard to credit them fairly.
assessment.maturity: Mature; the framework has been central for around 25 years, and it has been tested through the financial crisis and the post-pandemic inflation.
uncertainties: Hard to attribute credit with so many contributors.
Choosing between Taylor, Gertler, Christiano and Eichenbaum.
Debate over the framework's performance after 2008 and 2021.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamic panel GMM estimators are used across applied economics, enabling credible estimation with persistent data and fixed effects. This is a core methodological tool with very wide use.
assessment.attribution: The Arellano-Bond and Arellano-Bover/Blundell-Bond estimators are clearly credited to these three. The line of earlier work (Anderson-Hsiao, Holtz-Eakin-Newey-Rosen) is not in this entry, a possible omission.
assessment.maturity: More than thirty years of use. Known problems such as weak and many instruments are also well documented.
uncertainties: Precedence of earlier contributors.
Whether the committee regards this as a tool refinement rather than a conceptual advance.
Blundell has other contributions listed elsewhere.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This work reframed how technology and trade shape wages, employment and polarization. It combines a task-based framework with well-identified empirical studies of the China shock, and it shaped public debate.
assessment.attribution: Autor and Katz are linked to the technology and tasks strand, while Autor, Dorn and Hanson drive the China-shock evidence. Dorn is omitted under the cap, and the strands are not identical, which complicates credit.
assessment.maturity: Core papers are from 2003 to 2013. The long-run durability of the findings and their interpretation are still being tested.
uncertainties: Credit across the technology and trade strands.
Omission of Dorn.
Debate over the size of the China shock and the task framework's explanatory power.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population administrative data transformed the measurement of intergenerational mobility and neighbourhood effects, with large policy influence. The empirical advance is major and builds on administrative records and quasi-experiments.
assessment.attribution: Chetty is the central figure, with Hendren on the neighbourhood-effects work. Friedman and Katz contributed substantially, and credit within a large collaborative group is hard to apportion.
assessment.maturity: Mostly work from the 2010s and later. Replication, long-run follow-up and critiques of measurement are still developing, which makes it less mature than the older candidates.
uncertainties: Time needed for confirmation and replication.
Attribution within a large team.
Methodological critiques of neighbourhood-effect estimates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantile regression gives a way to study the whole conditional distribution rather than the mean, and it is widely used in labour, inequality and other applied fields. It is a lasting methodological contribution.
assessment.attribution: Koenker and Bassett's 1978 paper is the origin and is clearly credited. Chernozhukov's later extensions (inference, instrumental and high-dimensional quantiles) are important but are also listed under other candidates.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with almost fifty years of use, software and theory.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees it as a method of Nobel scale compared with a conceptual advance.
Chernozhukov's role in relation to other ballot entries.
Statistical origins of the technique.
